description.value: This voxel-based morphometric study identified neuroanatomical signatures of pathological sweet tooth and hyperphagia in individuals with frontotemporal lobar degeneration, using volumetric MRI and voxelwise grey matter analyses.

spans.text: In this voxel-based morphometric (VBM) study we demonstrate neuroanatomical signatures of different abnormalities of eating behaviour (pathological sweet tooth and increased food consumption, or hyperphagia) in individuals with frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD).

description.value: Sixteen male patients with FTLD and nine healthy age-matched male controls underwent volumetric brain MRI; the patient group was assessed for abnormal eating behaviours and compared with healthy controls, with additional covariate-only behavioural models within the FTLD group.

spans.text: Sixteen male patients with FTLD were assessed using the Manchester and Oxford Universities Scale for the Psychopathological Assessment of Dementia and classified according to the presence or absence of abnormal eating behaviours.

value: Compared with healthy controls, the FTLD group had extensive bilateral grey matter loss predominantly involving the frontal and temporal lobes, insula, and basal forebrain.
The distribution of atrophy was typical of that described previously in other VBM studies of FTLD.

value: Pathological sweet tooth was associated with reduced grey matter in a distributed network of brain areas, more extensive in the right cerebral hemisphere.

This network included the posterolateral OFC, dorsolateral prefrontal cortex and anterolateral temporal lobes bilaterally, and the anterior insula, parahippocampal and fusiform gyri and caudate nucleus in the right cerebral hemisphere.
Grey matter loss was significant after correction based on anatomical small volumes in bilateral OFC and right insula, but not in the right or left anterior temporal lobe.
We interpret the distinct pattern of grey matter loss as a signature of pathological sweet tooth.

value: Hyperphagia was associated with reduced grey matter in OFC bilaterally, in regions located more anteromedially than those implicated in association with pathological sweet tooth but lateral to gyrus rectus.
Grey matter loss associated with hyperphagia was not significant after small volume correction in OFC based on the a priori anatomical hypotheses.
We interpret the distinct pattern of grey matter loss as a signature of hyperphagia.

description.value: Images were normalized to a customised template, segmented into grey matter, white matter and cerebrospinal fluid, masked to exclude non-brain voxels, modulated and smoothed.

spans.text: All study images were normalised to this customised template and each normalised image was segmented into grey matter, white matter and cerebrospinal fluid using customised prior probability maps.
A VBM analysis was performed in SPM99 ( http://www.fil.ion.ucl.ac.uk/spm ) under Matlab 6®, using an optimised template-based method ( ) and MIDAS image analysis software ( ).
Grey matter images were modulated and smoothed with an isotropic Gaussian kernel of 8 mm FWHM.
